**What I changed:** Rebuilt the engine pylon (one code block inside the four-engine loop, so it applies to all four nacelles) in `benchmark/boeing747/candidates/terransoul-fable5-v2r2/plane.js`. The old pylon — a 0.45-thin, dark, axis-aligned box — became a 3.6 × 1.8 × 0.7 wedge in the light nacelle material, pitched 16° nose-down (`rotation.z = -0.28`) and repositioned to `(le + 0.9, under - 0.65, z)`.

**Why:** Both judge tracks call the engines "floating / not properly pylon-mounted / no visible pylons," yet the source already hangs the cowls 2.1 below the wing and 4.5 ahead of the leading edge — the placement iter 9/10 fixed. Inspecting the renders against the references showed the real root cause: the pylon was dark-on-dark against the wing and a 0.45 sliver edge-on, so it was invisible from every camera, leaving the light cowls reading as detached pods (top view: "upright cylinders atop wings"; close-up: a floating outboard engine counted as a mystery "extra"). Prior iterations changed pylon *size* but never its *visibility*. The new wedge is light-against-dark and raked like the real 747 pylon: it rises ~0.37 proud of the cowl crown ahead of the leading edge, wraps just over the razor LE (0.07 crest inboard / 0.24 outboard — the over-LE fairing you see in real top-down photos), and buries its aft-top corner in the wing diamond. I verified all box corners numerically at both span stations before editing: bottom edge embedded inside the cowl barrel, top edge piercing the wing skin, no floating corners, no coplanar faces — so craftsmanship shouldn't regress, and view 8's noted "engine pylon detail" imperfection is directly addressed.
